audit_scope.description: This audit covers both EL and CL logic and their interfaces. The subgraphs span EL networking protocol changes (eth/69-70), EL gas economics and consensus fork activation (Tangerine Whistle, Byzantium), EL byte utilities, CL light client sync protocol, CL P2P gossip/req-resp (Capella), CL validator slashing protection interchange, and wallet/DApp provider API boundaries (EIP-1102, EIP-1193, EIP-5593).

out_of_scope: Full EVM opcode implementation details beyond byte padding
Full beacon state transition beyond light client and Capella P2P scope

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, resource exhaustion attacks, unauthorized account access attempts, phishing via provider API
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks/transactions, request pre-PoS data to waste resources, exploit protocol version mismatch during transition

cl_vectors.threat: Propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, forge BLS-to-execution-change messages, surround voting

cl_vectors.source: Malicious Full Node / Light Client Server
cl_vectors.threat: Serve invalid bootstrap data, provide malicious LightClientUpdates, eclipse light clients

cl_vectors.entry_point: Checkpoint sync endpoint, interchange file import
cl_vectors.threat: Provide incorrect checkpoint data, supply tampered slashing protection files to enable slashable signing

misclassified_entities.reason: Parent block is internal blockchain state data, not an external entity. It is prior state within the system, not data arriving from outside the system boundary.
EVM instruction caller is an internal component of the execution layer, not an external entity. Byte padding is called by internal EVM operations.
Generic 'calling function' is an internal component. The security concern about untrusted size parameters is valid but the threat originates from external transaction data, not from internal callers.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer Node via devp2p (eth/69-70)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p eth/70 protocol messages (GetBlockBodies 0x05, BlockBodies 0x06, GetReceipts 0x0f, Receipts 0x10)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peers. Any node on the network can send protocol messages. Peers may request pre-PoS data or send malformed block data. No authentication mechanism in devp2p.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P block propagation (block headers with difficulty, block bodies, uncle headers)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners/block producers submit blocks over unauthenticated P2P network. Block difficulty, reward computations, and fork activation all depend on validating miner-produced blocks. Malicious miners could produce blocks with incorrect difficulty or attempt to trigger fork logic incorrectly.

trusted_external_entities.name: Attacker via Transaction Submission
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attackers craft transactions with many cheap IO operations to degrade network performance. EIP-608/EIP-150 gas repricing mitigates this but the entry point remains untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Full Node / Light Client Server via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Light client P2P req/resp (LightClientBootstrap, LightClientUpdatesByRange) and gossip (LightClientFinalityUpdate, LightClientOptimisticUpdate)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Full nodes serving light client data are unauthenticated P2P peers. A malicious full node could serve invalid bootstrap objects or updates. Trust derives only from cryptographic verification of sync committee signatures (2/3 honest assumption), not from the transport layer.

trusted_external_entities.name: Trusted Checkpoint Provider via External API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: External checkpoint sync endpoint (weak subjectivity checkpoint root)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The checkpoint source is external and unauthenticated. Despite being called 'trusted', the checkpoint provider is outside the system boundary and could supply a malicious finalized block root, bootstrapping the light client onto an invalid fork. Security relies on out-of-band trust assumptions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Gossip Network Peer via CL P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: GossipSub topics (bls_to_execution_change, beacon_block Capella fork digest)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL gossip peers are unauthenticated. They can send invalid BLS-to-execution-change messages, blocks with wrong fork digests, or duplicate messages. All content must be validated (epoch threshold, first-valid-per-validator, process_bls_to_execution_change, fork digest verification).

trusted_external_entities.name: Requesting Peer via CL Req/Resp
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote peers requesting blocks are unauthenticated. Server must correctly determine fork version for serialization. Malicious peers could request large ranges to cause resource exhaustion.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Node via Validator API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Validator client API (block signing requests, attestation signing requests)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The beacon node communicates with the validator client over a local authenticated channel. However, a compromised beacon node could request signatures on slashable messages. The validator client MUST independently verify all signing requests against its slashing protection database regardless of beacon node trust.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Operator via CLI/File Import
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Slashing protection interchange file import (EIP-3076 JSON format)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The validator operator provides interchange files during client migration. While the operator is assumed to be the legitimate owner, the file itself may have been exported from an untrusted source or tampered with. Full schema validation, genesis root verification, and BLS key validation are required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Previous Validator Client via Interchange File
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EIP-3076 JSON interchange file (signed_blocks, signed_attestations records)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The interchange file originates from a different validator client implementation. The file content is untrusted: it could be malformed, from a different network, or deliberately crafted to omit historical records enabling slashable signing. Full validation pipeline required.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Ethereum Provider API (window.ethereum)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps are untrusted web applications executing in the browser. They can invoke arbitrary RPC methods, request account access, and attempt to manipulate the provider. All input must be sanitized, rate-limited, and user consent required for sensitive operations.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious DApp via Provider API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Explicitly adversarial DApp attempting arbitrary operations on the Provider. Provider must maintain isolation from Wallet, contain no private data, and enforce rate limits.

trusted_external_entities.name: Browser User via Consent Dialog
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Wallet consent dialog (approve/reject account access), developer mode toggle
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The user is the legitimate owner making authorization decisions. However, users may be phished into approving malicious requests or enabling developer mode permanently. The system must present clear, accurate origin information.

trusted_external_entities.name: Third-Party Advertisement/Iframe
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Third-party iframes (ads, widgets) are untrusted and should be blocked from provider access by default. Only first-party same-origin iframes without restrictive sandbox or explicitly permissioned third-party iframes should gain access.

trusted_external_entities.name: Website/DApp Origin via Page Load
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Page load triggering secure context check (window.isSecureContext, origin trustworthiness)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any website can attempt to receive provider injection. Only secure contexts with trustworthy origins should receive the provider. Insecure HTTP origins (except localhost with dev mode) must be blocked.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethereum Network via Provider Connectivity
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network state changes arrive from remote infrastructure. A compromised or manipulated network connection could produce false connectivity events, incorrect chainId values, or denial of service.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: devp2p eth/70 Block Data Request Handler
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All incoming P2P requests must be validated for block number range (>= 15,537,393 for post-PoS). Pre-PoS data requests must be rejected. Message format must be validated against eth/70 protocol spec.
Block number scope validation required. Must reject requests targeting blocks below Paris upgrade boundary. Rate limiting on request volume to prevent resource exhaustion.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block validation pipeline (difficulty, reward, fork activation)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block header validation required: difficulty must match computed expected difficulty using EIP-649 rules (fake block number with 3M offset for post-Byzantium). Block reward must be exactly 3 ETH (post-Byzantium). Fork activation block numbers must be checked.

EIP-150 gas repricing must be applied for all IO-heavy operations (SLOAD, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, CALL, etc.) at post-Tangerine Whistle blocks (>= 2,463,000). Gas costs must accurately reflect computational cost to prevent DoS.

The checkpoint root must be verified against a trusted source (weak subjectivity assumption). The bootstrap object returned must be cryptographically verified against the checkpoint root. No authentication of the provider itself is possible.

All updates must be validated against sync committee signatures. At least 2/3 supermajority of sync committee signatures required. Finalized header advancement must be verified. Fork version transitions must be handled correctly.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Light client P2P req/resp (bootstrap, updates by range)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Responses from peers must be cryptographically verified. Multiple peers should be queried to prevent eclipse attacks. Connection to at least one honest full node assumed.
Must validate: (1) current_epoch >= CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH, (2) first valid change per validator index, (3) full process_bls_to_execution_change validation. Reject/ignore messages failing any check.
Fork digest must match expected Capella fork digest. Block contents including embedded bls_to_execution_changes must be fully validated.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: BeaconBlocksByRange v2 / BeaconBlocksByRoot v2 response handler
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Fork version must be correctly determined via compute_fork_version for each block's epoch. Serialization format must match the fork version. Incorrect fork-version mapping could cause deserialization failures or acceptance of malformed data.

Despite authenticated local channel, all signing requests must be checked against slashing protection DB. Block slot must be >= minimum previously signed slot. Attestation source/target epochs must be >= minimums. No surround voting. Missing signing roots treated as conflicts (conservative).

Validator must be completely stopped during import. File must pass JSON schema validation, genesis_validators_root must match current network, all BLS public keys must be valid, signing roots format verified.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EIP-3076 interchange file parser and validator
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full validation pipeline: JSON schema, genesis root match, BLS key validity, signing root format. Missing signing roots must be treated as potential conflicts (conservative interpretation). Duplicate public keys must be merged safely.
All request arguments must be validated (method field required). Input must be sanitized. Rate limiting enforced. Provider must not contain private data. Provider-Wallet isolation must be maintained.

Explicit user consent required before exposing any account addresses. Consent dialog must be browser-isolated from DApp manipulation. Origin must be accurately displayed. Permission caching must be per-origin.
Full input sanitization, rate limiting, Provider-Wallet isolation. Provider must contain no private user data. All methods requiring authorization must check permission state.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Wallet consent dialog / developer mode toggle
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Consent dialog must be isolated from DApp JavaScript. Origin displayed must be accurate (no spoofing). Developer mode must default to disabled. User must understand security implications of granting access.

Third-party iframes blocked by default. First-party iframes require sandbox compatibility check. Third-party access only via explicit Permissions API grant. Sandbox attribute must include allow-same-origin for first-party.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EIP-5593 secure context and origin trustworthiness check
boundary_edges.security_assumption: window.isSecureContext must be true. Origin must be potentially trustworthy per W3C Secure Contexts spec (HTTPS, localhost, file://). HTTP non-localhost blocked unless developer mode enabled.

chainId must be verified in hex format. Disconnect events must trigger appropriate error propagation (ProviderRpcError codes 4900/4901). Chain changes must be validated before emitting chainChanged events.
